summary: Serialized KV lock contention causing P99 latency spikes for identical short prompts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on dedicated capacity report intermittent high p99 inference latency when sending identical short prompts repeatedly (chat-style: same first user message). Impact is most visible for low-token prompts (<= 32 tokens).

Impact:
- NimbleDocs reports timeouts and visible lag in UI; automated tests show p99 jump from ~120ms to ~1.8s for identical prompt bursts.
- Affects production us-east dedicated pool for customer (single shard allocation).
- Customer productivity and demo reliability impacted; escalated to P1 due to enterprise SLA.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated, prod-us-east, single GPU shard pool pinned to customer tenant.
- Serving runtime version: 1.12.3 -> 1.13.0 (rolled out 2026-03-08).
- KV cache backend: prefix-kv v2, partitioned shards, per-tenant locks enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) On customer's dedicated endpoint, send 200 sequential requests using identical 12-token prompt at QPS ~20 (burst pattern: 5 concurrent clients issuing identical prompt).
2) Observe p50/p95 stable but p99 shows periodic spikes to ~1.8s and occasional 504 timeouts.
3) Reduce concurrency or change prompt content -> latency normalizes.

Observed logs and metrics:
- Serving runtime logs: repeated entries 'kv-lock: waiting for lease key=<prefix_hash>' with wait times 200-900ms.
- KV cache metrics: lock_acquire_latency p99 ~650ms after 1.13.0 rollout, previously <5ms.
- Trace spans: requests spend majority of time in 'kv:acquire_lock' then short in 'kv:fetch' and 'runtime:generate'.
- No increase in GPU utilization or host CPU; network I/O normal.

Hypothesis / initial findings:
- The 1.13.0 change enabled serialized per-prefix locking to avoid duplicate warmups; under identical prompt bursts this leads to queuing behind the first request's lock holder, amplifying tail latency.
- Impact amplified on dedicated single-shard tenants because many identical prompts map to same prefix shard and same lock key.
- TTL/eviction not primarily responsible: cache hit ratio remains high after warmup, but lock waits persist.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed correlation between rollout window of 1.13.0 and first customer reports (2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-09).
- Reproduced in staging by turning on 'serialize_prefix_warmup=true' flag and replaying identical prompt bursts; p99 jumps reproduced.
- Captured flame graphs showing blocked goroutines waiting on lock; stack traces point to kv/shard_lock.go:AcquireLease.
- Identified code change: PR 3342 introduced a global per-prefix mutex to coordinate warmups; intended to reduce duplicate kv-writes but not designed for high-concurrency identical prompt patterns.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Scoped bypass: set per-tenant feature flag 'serialize_prefix_warmup=false' for NimbleDocs -> immediate p99 improvement to baseline within 15 minutes.
- Increased shard parallelism for the tenant (provisioned an extra shard) -> reduced contention but required rebalancing and not ideal short-term.
- Implemented a client-side jitter recommendation for customer to avoid synchronized bursts (helpful but not acceptable long-term).

Planned next steps / remediation:
- Short-term: keep tenant feature flag disabled for affected customers while we patch. Notify SRE and CS to rollback flag for other impacted tenants as needed.
- Mid-term: implement optimistic lock with fast-path for cache-hit warmups (patch in progress: PR 3359). Expected timeline: patch + canary in staging 3 days, prod rollout 7 days after sign-off.
- Long-term: add metrics and dashboards for per-prefix lock wait time (alerting at p95>200ms) and add automated fallback to allow concurrent warmups beyond N waiters.

Resolution criteria:
- Reproduce case no longer shows p99 > 400ms under identical prompt bursts in staging and prod for customer after patch.
- Metrics and alerts added and verified.

Attachments / links:
- Stack traces and flame graphs: link in related_confluence_pages.
- Customer-reported timestamps and request IDs uploaded to support ticket thread.

public_status_message: We observed increased tail latency for some dedicated tenants due to serialized prefix locking introduced in a recent runtime release. A temporary flag was disabled for affected customers and a patch is being prepared to allow concurrent warmups while preventing duplicate writes. We'll update customers when the fix is rolled out.
